paragraphs.text: And he looked up, and saw the rich men that were casting their gifts into the treasury.
paragraphs.original: Ἀναβλέψας δὲ εἶδεν τοὺς βάλλοντας εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον τὰ δῶρα αὐτῶν πλουσίους.
paragraphs.translit: Anablepsas de eiden tous ballontas eis to gazophylakion ta dōra autōn plousious.

paragraphs.text: And he saw a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites.
paragraphs.original: εἶδεν δέ τινα χήραν πενιχρὰν βάλλουσαν ἐκεῖ λεπτὰ δύο,
paragraphs.translit: eiden de tina chēran penichran ballousan ekei lepta dyo,

paragraphs.text: And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, This poor widow cast in more than they all:
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν· Ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα ἡ πτωχὴ αὕτη πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν·
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen· Alēthōs legō hymin hoti hē chēra hē ptōchē hautē pleion pantōn ebalen·

paragraphs.text: for all these did of their superfluity cast in unto the gifts; but she of her want did cast in all the living that she had.
paragraphs.original: πάντες γὰρ οὗτοι ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον εἰς τὰ δῶρα, αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τοῦ ὑστερήματος αὐτῆς πάντα τὸν βίον ὃν εἶχεν ἔβαλεν.
paragraphs.translit: pantes gar houtoi ek tou perisseuontos autois ebalon eis ta dōra, hautē de ek tou hysterēmatos autēs panta ton bion hon eichen ebalen.

paragraphs.text: And as some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and offerings, he said,
paragraphs.original: Καί τινων λεγόντων περὶ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, ὅτι λίθοις καλοῖς καὶ ἀναθήμασιν κεκόσμηται εἶπεν·
paragraphs.translit: Kai tinōn legontōn peri tou hierou, hoti lithois kalois kai anathēmasin kekosmētai eipen·

paragraphs.text: As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in which there shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
paragraphs.original: Ταῦτα ἃ θεωρεῖτε, ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται λίθος ἐπὶ λίθῳ ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: Tauta ha theōreite, eleusontai hēmerai en hais ouk aphethēsetai lithos epi lithō hos ou katalythēsetai.

paragraphs.text: And they asked him, saying, Teacher, when therefore shall these things be? and what [shall be] the sign when these things are about to come to pass?
paragraphs.original: Ἐπηρώτησαν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, πότε οὖν ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα γίνεσθαι;
paragraphs.translit: Epērōtēsan de auton legontes· Didaskale, pote oun tauta estai, kai ti to sēmeion hotan mellē tauta ginesthai;

paragraphs.text: And he said, Take heed that ye be not led astray: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am [he]; and, The time is at hand: go ye not after them.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Βλέπετε μὴ πλανηθῆτε· πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες· Ἐγώ εἰμι καί· Ὁ καιρὸς ἤγγικεν· μὴ πορευθῆτε ὀπίσω αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Blepete mē planēthēte· polloi gar eleusontai epi tō onomati mou legontes· Egō eimi kai· Ho kairos ēngiken· mē poreuthēte opisō autōn.

paragraphs.text: And when ye shall hear of wars and tumults, be not terrified: for these things must needs come to pass first; but the end is not immediately.
paragraphs.original: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκαταστασίας, μὴ πτοηθῆτε· δεῖ γὰρ ταῦτα γενέσθαι πρῶτον, ἀλλʼ οὐκ εὐθέως τὸ τέλος.
paragraphs.translit: hotan de akousēte polemous kai akatastasias, mē ptoēthēte· dei gar tauta genesthai prōton, allʼ ouk eutheōs to telos.

paragraphs.text: Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom;
paragraphs.original: τότε ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγερθήσεται ἔθνος ἐπʼ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν,
paragraphs.translit: tote elegen autois· Egerthēsetai ethnos epʼ ethnos kai basileia epi basileian,

paragraphs.text: and there shall be great earthquakes, and in divers places famines and pestilences; and there shall be terrors and great signs from heaven.
paragraphs.original: σεισμοί τε μεγάλοι καὶ κατὰ τόπους λιμοὶ καὶ λοιμοὶ ἔσονται, φόβητρά τε καὶ σημεῖα ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ μεγάλα ἔσται.
paragraphs.translit: seismoi te megaloi kai kata topous limoi kai loimoi esontai, phobētra te kai sēmeia apʼ ouranou megala estai.

paragraphs.text: But before all these things, they shall lay their hands on you, and shall persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues and prisons, bringing you before kings and governors for my name`s sake.
paragraphs.original: Πρὸ δὲ τούτων πάντων ἐπιβαλοῦσιν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν καὶ διώξουσιν, παραδιδόντες εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ φυλακάς, ἀπαγομένους ἐπὶ βασιλεῖς καὶ ἡγεμόνας ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου·
paragraphs.translit: Pro de toutōn pantōn epibalousin ephʼ hymas tas cheiras autōn kai diōxousin, paradidontes eis tas synagōgas kai phylakas, apagomenous epi basileis kai hēgemonas heneken tou onomatos mou·

paragraphs.text: It shall turn out unto you for a testimony.
paragraphs.original: ἀποβήσεται ὑμῖν εἰς μαρτύριον.
paragraphs.translit: apobēsetai hymin eis martyrion.

paragraphs.text: Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate beforehand how to answer:
paragraphs.original: θέτε οὖν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν μὴ προμελετᾶν ἀπολογηθῆναι,
paragraphs.translit: thete oun en tais kardiais hymōn mē promeletan apologēthēnai,

paragraphs.text: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to withstand or to gainsay.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ γὰρ δώσω ὑμῖν στόμα καὶ σοφίαν ᾗ οὐ δυνήσονται ἀντιστῆναι ἢ ἀντειπεῖν ἅπαντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: egō gar dōsō hymin stoma kai sophian hē ou dynēsontai antistēnai ē anteipein hapantes hoi antikeimenoi hymin.

paragraphs.text: But ye shall be delivered up even by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolk, and friends; and [some] of you shall they cause to be put to death.
paragraphs.original: παραδοθήσεσθε δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ γονέων καὶ ἀδελφῶν καὶ συγγενῶν καὶ φίλων, καὶ θανατώσουσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: paradothēsesthe de kai hypo goneōn kai adelphōn kai syngenōn kai philōn, kai thanatōsousin ex hymōn,

paragraphs.text: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name`s sake.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.
paragraphs.translit: kai esesthe misoumenoi hypo pantōn dia to onoma mou.

paragraphs.text: And not a hair of your head shall perish.
paragraphs.original: καὶ θρὶξ ἐκ τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν οὐ μὴ ἀπόληται.
paragraphs.translit: kai thrix ek tēs kephalēs hymōn ou mē apolētai.

paragraphs.text: In your patience ye shall win your souls.
paragraphs.original: ἐν τῇ ὑπομονῇ ὑμῶν κτήσασθε τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: en tē hypomonē hymōn ktēsasthe tas psychas hymōn.

paragraphs.text: But when ye see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that her desolation is at hand.
paragraphs.original: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε κυκλουμένην ὑπὸ στρατοπέδων Ἰερουσαλήμ, τότε γνῶτε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ ἐρήμωσις αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Hotan de idēte kykloumenēn hypo stratopedōn Ierousalēm, tote gnōte hoti ēngiken hē erēmōsis autēs.

paragraphs.text: Then let them that are in Judaea flee unto the mountains; and let them that are in the midst of her depart out; and let not them that are in the country enter therein.
paragraphs.original: τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη, καὶ οἱ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς ἐκχωρείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἐν ταῖς χώραις μὴ εἰσερχέσθωσαν εἰς αὐτήν,
paragraphs.translit: tote hoi en tē Ioudaia pheugetōsan eis ta orē, kai hoi en mesō autēs ekchōreitōsan, kai hoi en tais chōrais mē eiserchesthōsan eis autēn,

paragraphs.text: For these are days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἡμέραι ἐκδικήσεως αὗταί εἰσιν τοῦ πλησθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα.
paragraphs.translit: hoti hēmerai ekdikēseōs hautai eisin tou plēsthēnai panta ta gegrammena.

paragraphs.text: Woe unto them that are with child and to them that give suck in those days! for there shall be great distress upon the land, and wrath unto this people.
paragraphs.original: οὐαὶ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις· ἔσται γὰρ ἀνάγκη μεγάλη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὀργὴ τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ,
paragraphs.translit: ouai tais en gastri echousais kai tais thēlazousais en ekeinais tais hēmerais· estai gar anankē megalē epi tēs gēs kai orgē tō laō toutō,

paragraphs.text: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led captive into all the nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πεσοῦνται στόματι μαχαίρης καὶ αἰχμαλωτισθήσονται εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πάντα, καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἔσται πατουμένη ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν, ἄχρι οὗ πληρωθῶσιν καιροὶ ἐθνῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai pesountai stomati machairēs kai aichmalōtisthēsontai eis ta ethnē panta, kai Ierousalēm estai patoumenē hypo ethnōn, achri hou plērōthōsin kairoi ethnōn.

paragraphs.text: And there shall be signs in sun and moon and stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, in perplexity for the roaring of the sea and the billows;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔσονται σημεῖα ἐν ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ καὶ ἄστροις, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς συνοχὴ ἐθνῶν ἐν ἀπορίᾳ ἤχους θαλάσσης καὶ σάλου,
paragraphs.translit: Kai esontai sēmeia en hēliō kai selēnē kai astrois, kai epi tēs gēs synochē ethnōn en aporia ēchous thalassēs kai salou,

paragraphs.text: men fainting for fear, and for expectation of the things which are coming on the world: for the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.
paragraphs.original: ἀποψυχόντων ἀνθρώπων ἀπὸ φόβου καὶ προσδοκίας τῶν ἐπερχομένων τῇ οἰκουμένῃ, αἱ γὰρ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: apopsychontōn anthrōpōn apo phobou kai prosdokias tōn eperchomenōn tē oikoumenē, hai gar dynameis tōn ouranōn saleuthēsontai.

paragraphs.text: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλῃ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai tote opsontai ton hyion tou anthrōpou erchomenon en nephelē meta dynameōs kai doxēs pollēs.

paragraphs.text: But when these things begin to come to pass, look up, and lift up your heads; because your redemption draweth nigh.
paragraphs.original: ἀρχομένων δὲ τούτων γίνεσθαι ἀνακύψατε καὶ ἐπάρατε τὰς κεφαλὰς ὑμῶν, διότι ἐγγίζει ἡ ἀπολύτρωσις ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: archomenōn de toutōn ginesthai anakypsate kai eparate tas kephalas hymōn, dioti engizei hē apolytrōsis hymōn.

paragraphs.text: And he spake to them a parable: Behold the fig tree, and all the trees:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἶπεν παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς· Ἴδετε τὴν συκῆν καὶ πάντα τὰ δένδρα·
paragraphs.translit: Kai eipen parabolēn autois· Idete tēn sykēn kai panta ta dendra·

paragraphs.text: when they now shoot forth, ye see it and know of your own selves that the summer is now nigh.
paragraphs.original: ὅταν προβάλωσιν ἤδη, βλέποντες ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤδη ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·
paragraphs.translit: hotan probalōsin ēdē, blepontes aphʼ heautōn ginōskete hoti ēdē engys to theros estin·

paragraphs.text: Even so ye also, when ye see these things coming to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai hymeis, hotan idēte tauta ginomena, ginōskete hoti engys estin hē basileia tou theou.

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all things be accomplished.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin hoti ou mē parelthē hē genea hautē heōs an panta genētai.

paragraphs.text: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.
paragraphs.original: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρελεύσονται.
paragraphs.translit: ho ouranos kai hē gē pareleusontai, hoi de logoi mou ou mē pareleusontai.

paragraphs.text: But take heed to yourselves, lest haply your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day come on you suddenly as a snare:
paragraphs.original: Προσέχετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς μήποτε βαρηθῶσιν ὑμῶν αἱ καρδίαι ἐν κραιπάλῃ καὶ μέθῃ καὶ μερίμναις βιωτικαῖς, καὶ ἐπιστῇ ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς αἰφνίδιος ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη
paragraphs.translit: Prosechete de heautois mēpote barēthōsin hymōn hai kardiai en kraipalē kai methē kai merimnais biōtikais, kai epistē ephʼ hymas aiphnidios hē hēmera ekeinē

paragraphs.text: for [so] shall it come upon all them that dwell on the face of all the earth.
paragraphs.original: ὡς παγίς· ἐπεισελεύσεται γὰρ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: hōs pagis· epeiseleusetai gar epi pantas tous kathēmenous epi prosōpon pasēs tēs gēs.

paragraphs.text: But watch ye at every season, making supplication, that ye may prevail to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.
paragraphs.original: ἀγρυπνεῖτε δὲ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ δεόμενοι ἵνα κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, καὶ σταθῆναι ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: agrypneite de en panti kairō deomenoi hina katischysēte ekphygein tauta panta ta mellonta ginesthai, kai stathēnai emprosthen tou hyiou tou anthrōpou.

paragraphs.text: And every day he was teaching in the temple; and every night he went out, and lodged in the mount that is called Olivet.
paragraphs.original: Ἦν δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων, τὰς δὲ νύκτας ἐξερχόμενος ηὐλίζετο εἰς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν·
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de tas hēmeras en tō hierō didaskōn, tas de nyktas exerchomenos ēulizeto eis to oros to kaloumenon Elaiōn·

paragraphs.text: And all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple, to hear him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ὤρθριζεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai pas ho laos ōrthrizen pros auton en tō hierō akouein autou.
